Presbycusis, also referred to as age-related hearing loss (ARHL), is a multifaceted condition caused by the natural aging process affecting the auditory system. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in human populations can identify potential genes linked to ARHL. Despite this, our knowledge of the biochemical and molecular mechanisms behind the condition remains incomplete. This study aims to evaluate a potential protective tool for ARHL treatment by comparing human blood-based target gene-miRNA associations regulated in ARHL. To identify promising target genes for ARHL, we utilized an mRNA assay. To determine the role of miRNA in ARHL, we investigated the expression profile of miRNA in whole blood in ARHL patients with real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). A reporter gene assay was performed to confirm the regulation of candidate genes by microRNA. Through RT-qPCR validation analysis, we finally confirmed the relationship between ARHL and the role of the interferon-gamma (IFNG) gene. This gene can be regarded as an age-related gene. Through gene ontology (GO) analysis, it has been found that these genes are enriched in pathways related to apoptosis. Among them, IFNG induces an inflammatory response, apoptotic cell death, and cellular senescence. We found that miR-409-3p downregulates the expression of the IFNG in vitro. In addition, the downregulation of the IFNG by miRNA 409-3p promoted cell apoptosis and suppressed proliferation. In conclusion, our study produced gene signatures and associated microRNA regulation that could be a protective key for ARHL patients. Introduction Inflammation has become a focal point in biomedical research on age-related conditions. As tissues age, the body undergoes a process called ‘chronic inflammation’. This low-grade, age-related inflammation, also known as ‘inflammaging’, progressively worsens over time [ 1 ]. Recently, the potential pathways of inflammation and its effect on age-related hearing loss (ARHL) have received more and more attention in the field of hearing research. Although the cochlea was traditionally thought to be an immune-privileged organ [ 2 ], recent research has demonstrated its susceptibility to systemic inflammation [ 3 , 4 ]. Prolonged activation of inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1α, IL-2, TNF-α, and NF-κB, which play critical roles in initiating, regulating, and amplifying immune responses, can penetrate cells within the inner ear, such as those in the endolymphatic sac [ 5 , 6 ]. Verschuur et al. conducted human studies that demonstrated a link between hearing thresholds and key serum biomarkers of low-grade inflammation [ 7 ]. They found associations between the average hearing thresholds in elderly individuals and their levels of IL-6, C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell counts, and neutrophil counts. Lowthian et al. also highlighted the potential therapeutic advantages of low-dose aspirin, a mild anti-inflammatory agent, for ARHL [ 8 ]. This finding adds to the growing body of evidence suggesting that chronic inflammatory processes are key mechanisms behind age-related conditions. One promising method for identifying genetic variants that contribute to ARHL is the use of a genome-wide association study (GWAS), which screens a large number of genetic markers throughout the genome for associations with the trait of interest. Trpchevska et al. performed a meta-analysis of GWASs in a large sample of 723,266 individuals who had self-reported or clinically diagnosed hearing impairment [ 9 ]. The study identified a total of 48 loci that were significantly associated with hearing impairment, including 10 loci that had not been previously reported. Additionally, Ivarsdottir et al. demonstrated that a combined cohort from Iceland and the UK Biobank (totaling 121,934 individuals identified through pure-tone audiograms and self-reported hearing difficulties) revealed 21 new associations, including 13 rare variants [ 10 ]. This study performed analysis for RNA sequencing data from ARHL patients and found 11 genes related to ARHL. MicroRNA(miRNA)s are a class of small, non-coding RNA molecules that occur naturally within organisms. Typically, miRNAs are 20–23 nucleotides long, and they function by binding to specific target messenger RNA (mRNA) transcripts via complementary base pairing [ 11 ]. The interaction between miRNAs and their target mRNA molecules can lead to gene silencing, translational repression, or target degradation. It is estimated that miRNAs have the potential to target up to 60% of all genes, and each miRNA can affect the expression of hundreds of target genes [ 12 ]. Recent studies have revealed differences in miRNA expression in the inner ear of two mouse strains, C57BL/6J and CBA/J, which are frequently used in research on aging and age-related diseases due to the unavailability of human-derived samples. In the context of age-related hearing loss (ARHL), 111 miRNAs in C57 mice and 71 miRNAs in CBA mice showed differential expression [ 13 ]. Among these, downregulated miRNAs were more common than upregulated ones. Zhang’s research further identified miRNAs associated with the aging of the cochlear duct’s lateral wall, in addition to the organ of Corti. Downregulated miRNAs, such as those from the miR-183 and miR-181 families, were linked to proliferation and differentiation pathways [ 14 ], whereas upregulated miRNAs, including members of the miR-29 and miR-34 families, were implicated in pathways that activate or enhance apoptosis, involving genes like p53, p27, and Bcl2 [ 15 ]. While miRNAs are recognized for their roles in regulating cellular proliferation, differentiation, and growth within the inner ear, their function in the blood concerning age-related hearing loss (ARHL) remains unestablished. Zhuoran et al. suggested that miR-155 selectively interacts with the 3′untranslated region (3′UTR) of Stat1, leading to the suppression of mRNA expression. Additionally, the absence of miR-155 leads to the depression of IFN-γ-related transcription factors, offering a potential explanation for the heightened IFN response observed in microglia lacking miR-155 [ 16 ]. Amado T et al.’s research uncovered that within CD8+ T cells, miR-181a constrains the production of IFN-γ by repressing the expression of the transcription factor Id2, consequently fostering the activation of the IFNG expression program [ 17 ]. In another study, the miRNA expression pattern was analyzed in melanoma cells undergoing IFN-γ-induced ferroptosis. Subsequently, Weinan et al. demonstrated that the upregulation of miR-21-3p enhances IFN-γ-triggered ferroptosis by promoting lipid peroxidation [ 18 ]. In the present study, we identified 11 potential genes by analyzing RNA sequencing from ARHL patients. Among the identified genes, we focused on the profiles of the IFNG gene, which is possibly involved in cochlear inflammation or ARHL. Moreover, we assessed the preventive role of miR-409-3p on the expression of the IFNG gene.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated human blood-based target gene-miRNA associations in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) to identify potential protective mechanisms. Through transcriptome analysis of human blood samples (whole blood and PBMCs) from 12 ARHL patients and 12 normal hearing controls, and in vitro experiments on HEI-OC-1 cells, the study identified molecular changes. It confirmed the upregulation of IFNG in ARHL patients and demonstrated that miR-409-3p is significantly downregulated in ARHL and inversely correlates with IFNG. miR-409-3p was shown to downregulate both IFNG and p16 expression in vitro, a mechanism that promotes cell apoptosis and suppresses proliferation, suggesting a protective role for miR-409-3p in ARHL pathogenesis.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Investigation of molecular mechanisms in age-related hearing loss (ARHL), involving an observational comparison of ARHL patients and normal hearing controls, complemented by in vitro cell treatments.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily involved an observational comparison between 12 ARHL patients and 12 normal hearing controls for gene and miRNA expression profiles. In vitro experiments on HEI-OC-1 cells included treatments with IFN-γ and miR-409-3p, but specific doses or dose-response comparisons for these cell treatments were not detailed. No specific therapeutic doses or durations were applied to human subjects, as the study focused on mechanistic analysis and target identification.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human blood (whole blood, PBMCs), HEI-OC-1 cells
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript (mRNA expression), Protein Level (cytokine activity)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher in ARHL patients, but lower when regulated by miR-409-3p.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Exhibited statistically significant upregulation (adjusted p < 0.05, at least two-fold) in whole blood and PBMCs from ARHL patients compared to normal hearing controls. Its expression decreased with increasing miR-409-3p concentration in HEI-OC-1 cells. Frequency of T cells producing IFN-γ was significantly increased in 25% of PBMCs from patients with autoimmune sensorineural hearing loss. IFN-γ treatment also causes upregulation of p16 and p15 in most cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytokine involved in tissue homeostasis, orchestrating immune and inflammatory responses, tumor immunity surveillance, induction of premature senescence, apoptotic cell death, and cellular senescence. It also sensitizes cochlear cells to cytotoxicity and is directly regulated by miR-409-3p.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Upregulated in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) and autoimmune sensorineural hearing loss, contributing to ARHL pathophysiology, cellular senescence, and chronic inflammation. Directly regulated by miR-409-3p in HEI-OC-1 cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Plays a significant role in ARHL pathogenesis and is regarded as an age-related gene. Its upregulation indicates involvement in age-related diseases and chronic inflammation, sensitizing cochlear cells to harmful effects. Its regulation by miR-409-3p suggests potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target for ARHL.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human blood (whole blood, PBMCs), HEI-OC-1 cells

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly lower in ARHL patients (inversely correlated with IFNG); upregulated in senescent endothelial progenitor cells.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated (* p < 0.05) in whole blood and HEI-OC-1 cells from ARHL patients compared to normal hearing controls. Its overexpression downregulates IFNG and p16 expression. Concurrent upregulation with miR-30a-5p can replicate cellular senescence.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates gene expression by possessing a binding site in the 3'UTR of IFNG, leading to the downregulation of IFNG and p16 signaling. This promotes cell apoptosis, suppresses proliferation, and is involved in cellular senescence. It also functions as a negative regulator of angiogenesis by targeting PPP2CA.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Significantly downregulated in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) patients, showing an inverse correlation with IFNG. It directly regulates IFNG and p16 expression in HEI-OC-1 cells and is implicated in cellular senescence and hearing loss pathogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Plays a significant role in ARHL pathogenesis and serves as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for human aging and hearing loss. Its downregulation is associated with ARHL, and its regulatory role suggests a protective mechanism by influencing inflammation, apoptosis, and cellular senescence.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower when regulated by miR-409-3p; higher when induced by IFN-γ or with prolonged expression.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression decreased as miR-409-3p concentration increased, indicating miR-409-3p induced downregulation. IFN-γ treatment causes upregulation of p16 and p15 in most cell types, and prolonged p16 expression induces cellular senescence.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Main factor responsible for accelerated cellular senescence. It functions as a tumor suppressor by forming a direct binding interaction with CDK4/6, preventing Rb phosphorylation, initiating G1 to S phase growth arrest, and inhibiting CDK activity. It is regulated by miR-409-3p.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Involved in age-related hearing loss (ARHL) and auditory dysfunction, acting as a senescence marker in HEI-OC-1 cells. Its expression is modulated by miR-409-3p and IFN-γ.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Its expression indicates cellular senescence and is associated with auditory dysfunction, including ARHL. Its regulation by miR-409-3p suggests involvement in ARHL mechanisms and the balance between tumor suppression and senescence.
